entities.label: JUDGE

sentences.text:
This appeal is filed against the award of the Tribunal in MVC No.125/2022 dated 28.08.2023 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T - II at Yadgiri (for short 'the Tribunal').
2.
Injured/claimant aged 20 years met with the accident on 19.09.2021 and filed a claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.37,00,000/-.
But, the Tribunal after considering entire evidence on record, dismissed the application.
3. Aggrieved by the said order, this appeal is preferred in which it is contended that, the accident was occurred between two wheeler and the bus and it is a head-on-collision.
The appellant sustained multiple fractures/injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the conductor of the bus gave a complaint stating that appellant was negligent in causing the accident.
But, the chargesheet was filed against both the drivers and the Tribunal without considering the same, dismissed the claim petition.
Therefore, requested this court for remanding the matter to the Tribunal.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7401 HC-KAR 4.

The perusal of the record shows that, on 19.09.2021, the appellant was proceeding on moped bearing registration No.KA-33-W-1846 and the bus bearing registration No.KA-33-F-0236 came from the opposite direction in rash and negligent manner and dashed the appellant.
As a result, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Further, as per the contention of the counsel for the appellant, after the investigation, the charge sheet was filed against both the vehicles, but the Tribunal observed that the appellant has not discharged his burden to show that the accident occurred only due to the rash and negligence of the driver of the bus and accordingly, dismissed the application.

Hence, this Court finds it reasonable to remand the matter to the Tribunal.
5.

In view of the above discussion, this appeal is allowed and remanded to the Tribunal, with a specific direction to grant a reasonable opportunity to both sides for adducing evidence and to advance arguments and to dispose of the matter within three months from the date of this order by duly considering the entire evidence on record on merits.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7401 HC-KAR 6.
Registry is directed to send the records within a period of ten days from today.
